Prompt: Write a cold email to [PROSPECT ROLE] at a [COMPANY TYPE] with [HEADCOUNT] people. Open with a specific problem my offer solves ([OFFER]), reference something real about them ([WHAT I NOTICED]), and ask for one low-commitment reply. Under 110 words, no compliment openers, no 'I hope this finds you well'.
Variables to Fill: COMPANY TYPE, HEADCOUNT, OFFER, PROSPECT ROLE, WHAT I NOTICED
When To Use It: You have a list of prospects and nothing to send them
Expected Output: 3 subject-line options + email body + one-sentence P.S. variant

Prompt: Take this generic cold email and rewrite it 4 ways: curiosity-driven, blunt-direct, data-led, and self-deprecating. Tell me which one fits a [INDUSTRY] buyer and why the other three lose. Paste email: [PASTE EMAIL]
When To Use It: Your first draft reads like every other sales email
Expected Output: 4 rewrites + a recommendation with reasoning

Prompt: Build a 4-touch follow-up sequence for [OFFER] aimed at [CUSTOMER]. Day 0 is the cold email. Each later touch must add genuinely new information (a number, an example, an objection answered) rather than 'just checking in'.
When To Use It: You keep sending 'following up' and getting nothing
Expected Output: 4 emails with send-day, subject, body, and what's new in each

Prompt: I am about to call [PROSPECT] at [COMPANY]. Here is everything I know: [WHAT I KNOW]. Give me an opening 20 seconds that is not a pitch, 5 discovery questions ordered from safest to hardest, and the 3 questions that would qualify them out early so I stop wasting time.
When To Use It: Pre-call prep, every single time
Expected Output: Opener script + ranked question list + disqualify questions

Prompt: Turn these rough call notes into a follow-up email that restates what they said, the one thing they care about most, and a next step with a specific time. Notes: [PASTE NOTES]
When To Use It: Right after any sales call, while memory is fresh
Expected Output: Email under 120 words + proposed meeting slot

Prompt: Here is an objection a prospect raised: [OBJECTION]. Give me the honest answer when the objection is true, the reframe when it is not, a question that turns it back to them, and the line I should stop using because it sounds defensive.
When To Use It: Mid-call, or rehearsing before a hard conversation
Expected Output: 4 labelled responses + a note on when to walk away

Prompt: Write a direct LinkedIn message to [ROLE] that references their post about [TOPIC] and moves toward a conversation about [OFFER]. No pitch in the first message, no 'thanks for connecting', under 60 words.
When To Use It: Warm-ish outreach where you've actually read their content
Expected Output: Message + 2 alternate first lines

Prompt: Segment this lead list into who to call today, who to send a nurture email to, and who to drop entirely. Score each on deal size, signal of intent, and fit. List: [PASTE LEADS]
When To Use It: You have 200 rows in a spreadsheet and two hours
Expected Output: Table with tier, reason, and recommended next action per lead

Prompt: Draft a re-engagement email to [CUSTOMER TYPE] who went quiet [TIMEFRAME] ago. Reference what they did while active, name the specific outcome they didn't reach, and offer one way back that costs them under 10 minutes.
When To Use It: Your best asset is a list of people who already said yes once
Expected Output: Email + subject + the one offer to lead with

Prompt: Create a proposal structure for [SERVICE] priced at [PRICE] for [CLIENT]. Must include the problem in their words, the outcome, the scope in bullets, an explicit not-in-scope list, the timeline, and why me. No filler sections.
When To Use It: Every deal above [PRICE] deserves a written proposal
Expected Output: Section-by-section outline with the sentence to open each one with

Prompt: Here is my proposal text: [PASTE PROPOSAL]. Rewrite it to sell the outcome, not the hours. Then list the 3 places where a cautious buyer would still feel unsure, and what evidence fixes each.
When To Use It: Before sending anything you want signed
Expected Output: Revised proposal + 3 gap notes with the evidence to add

Prompt: Write a 90-second discovery call opener for [BUSINESS TYPE] that sets the agenda, tells them what they'll get for their time, and gives permission to say no. Then list the 5 signals that mean this person is not my buyer.
When To Use It: You keep getting dragged into unstructured sales chats
Expected Output: Script + disqualifier checklist

Prompt: Turn one happy-customer result into 3 outreach assets: a LinkedIn post, a cold-email proof line, and a one-sentence case summary. Facts only from this: [RESULT DETAILS]
When To Use It: You have proof but haven't converted it into messaging
Expected Output: 3 assets + a note on which claim needs customer permission first

Prompt: Build a win-back offer for [CUSTOMER] who left for [REASON]. It must be time-boxed, cheaper for them than switching back costs, and honest about what we changed. Then give me the email.
When To Use It: A churned customer is 5x cheaper to reopen than a stranger
Expected Output: Offer definition + email + expiration wording

Prompt: I need to ask [PARTNER TYPE] for referrals without sounding transactional. Write the ask for a [INDUSTRY] context, plus 3 ways to make it easy for them to actually do it (a forwardable blurb, an intro email they can send unchanged, a shared incentive).
When To Use It: Your network already knows people who need this
Expected Output: The ask message + 3 ready-to-use referral enablers

Prompt: Write 10 content ideas for [CUSTOMER] who struggles with [PAIN]. Mix formats: 4 short posts, 3 long-form angles, 2 teaching pieces, 1 contrarian take. Each idea must state the specific belief it changes, not just the topic.
When To Use It: Content calendar planning, when you're posting but not saying anything
Expected Output: Table: idea, format, belief changed, first line

Prompt: Turn this long article into 6 platform-native pieces: 1 LinkedIn post, 1 X thread, 2 short-form video scripts, 1 newsletter intro, 1 community-friendly post. Paste: [ARTICLE]
When To Use It: You wrote something good once and let it die in one place
Expected Output: 6 versions, each respecting that platform's length and rhythm

Prompt: Write 12 hooks for [TOPIC] in these styles: number-led, question, confession, warning, myth-bust, before/after, quote, cost, timeline, blunt, odd detail, direct address. Then rank the 3 strongest for [CHANNEL] and say why.
When To Use It: You have a good body and a dead opening
Expected Output: 12 hooks + top-3 verdict

Prompt: Rewrite this copy so it sounds like a person talking to one friend: cut adjectives, replace abstractions with specifics, shorten sentences, kill every banned word (unlock, elevate, seamless, game-changer, cutting-edge). Text: [PASTE COPY]
When To Use It: Any draft that reads corporate
Expected Output: Rewrite + a line-by-line list of what you changed and why

Prompt: Build a 30-day content plan for [BUSINESS TYPE] with 3 posts a week. Each week must have one post that teaches, one that proves (case or data), one that sells. Include the topic and format for all 12.
When To Use It: You need a rhythm you can actually keep, not a wish list
Expected Output: 12-slot calendar with objective per post

Prompt: Give me 10 questions about [PAIN] in the exact words a real customer would type into Google or an AI chat, ordered from unaware to ready-to-buy. Under each, the one piece of content that answers it.
When To Use It: SEO briefs, bottom-of-funnel content, ad keyword lists
Expected Output: 10 queries + matching content angle

Prompt: Write a 6-email newsletter welcome sequence for subscribers who joined for [LEAD MAGNET]. Deliver something useful in 1 and 2, tell the origin story in 3, show proof in 4, present [OFFER] in 5, close honestly in 6.
When To Use It: You have subscribers and no sequence
Expected Output: 6 emails with send-day, subject, goal, body

Prompt: Audit this landing page against the 7 things that decide whether people read past the first screen: clarity, relevance, specificity, proof, friction, risk reversal, next step. Page: [URL OR PASTE COPY]
When To Use It: Traffic arrives but nobody converts
Expected Output: Scored list + the 3 fixes that would move the number most

Prompt: Write product descriptions for [PRODUCT] for three audiences: someone buying it for themselves, someone gifting it, someone comparing it to [COMPETITOR]. Different reasons, different words, same facts.
When To Use It: One product, many buyers who want different things
Expected Output: 3 descriptions + the headline claim each leans on

Prompt: Turn my service into a named framework with 4 stages, each with a one-line description, an outcome, and an artifact the client receives. My service: [SERVICE DESCRIPTION]
When To Use It: You're selling undifferentiated work and your price reflects that
Expected Output: Framework name, 4 stages, plus how to use it in a pitch

Prompt: Write 5 short-video scripts about [TOPIC]. Structure each as hook (3s), tension (10s), turn (25s), payoff (10s), and one line that gets comments. Include what to show on screen.
When To Use It: Repurposing written expertise into video without a studio
Expected Output: 5 scripts with timing and visual cues

Prompt: Create a testimonial request I can send to [HAPPY CUSTOMER] that gets a specific result instead of 'great to work with'. Include the 4 questions to ask, and a permission line for public use.
When To Use It: You have happy customers and no usable proof
Expected Output: The ask message + 4 questions + a template to tidy their reply into

Prompt: Write a contrarian opinion post about [COMMON ADVICE IN MY INDUSTRY]. State who the advice is wrong for, what to do instead, and the strongest argument against my own position. No outrage tone.
When To Use It: You want to be known for a view, not just for posting
Expected Output: Post + steelman paragraph + the risk of publishing it

Prompt: Build a lead magnet for [CUSTOMER] around [TOPIC]. It must be usable in under 15 minutes, deliver one outcome, and naturally point at [OFFER]. Give me the format, the outline, and the promise line.
When To Use It: Your freebie gets downloads but no buyers
Expected Output: Format + outline + headline + the follow-up email that connects it to the paid offer

Prompt: Here are 8 of my raw customer messages: [PASTE MESSAGES]. Pull the recurring phrases, complaints, and desired outcomes, then write the exact words I should use in my headline and first paragraph.
When To Use It: Voice-of-customer research you already have sitting unread
Expected Output: Phrase inventory + recommended headline and lead paragraph

Prompt: Write a [TYPE] email to [AUDIENCE] about [SUBJECT]. Keep it under 150 words, one idea, one ask, plain sentence structure. No 'just checking in', no 'per my last email'.
When To Use It: The emails you put off because you hate writing them
Expected Output: Email + 3 subject options, one being the plainest

Prompt: Rewrite this email to be 40% shorter while keeping every commitment and date intact, and moving the ask to the first two lines. Text: [PASTE EMAIL]
When To Use It: Your emails get skimmed and the ask gets missed
Expected Output: Tightened email + a note on what was cut

Prompt: Write 5 subject lines for [NEWSLETTER TOPIC] in these registers: curiosity, specific benefit, number, warning, personal. Flag which one is closest to clickbait for this audience and why.
When To Use It: Open rates are flat
Expected Output: 5 subject lines + a preheader for the winner

Prompt: Turn this messy bullet dump into a clear update for [RECIPIENT] that separates what's done, what's at risk, what I need from them, and the next date. Paste: [BULLETS]
When To Use It: Status updates, weekly reports, handovers
Expected Output: Structured update under 180 words with one bolded ask

Prompt: Write a difficult email: I need to tell [PERSON] that [UNPLEASANT TRUTH]. Direct, kind, no over-apologising, no hidden blame, states the consequence and the path forward. Under 160 words.
When To Use It: Late delivery, cancellation, price rise, a mistake you made
Expected Output: Email + 2 alternate openings (soft and firm)

Prompt: Draft a 3-step escalation for [PARTNER TYPE] who hasn't delivered [THING OWED]: polite reminder, clear deadline with consequence, final notice. Same facts each time, rising firmness.
When To Use It: Someone is blocking your work and you don't want a fight
Expected Output: 3 emails with the timing between them

Prompt: Write a cold-inquiry email that gets a reply from someone at a big company about [SPECIFIC THING]. Make the ask small, specific, and flatter their expertise rather than their status.
When To Use It: You need information or a meeting you can't buy
Expected Output: Email + a follow-up for day 7 assuming silence

Prompt: Reply to this customer email in a way that solves the problem and protects my time. Their email: [PASTE EMAIL]. My constraints: [CONSTRAINTS].
When To Use It: Inbox triage on the emails that cost hours
Expected Output: Reply + 1 alternate if I want to decline part of the ask

Prompt: Write an apology for [MISTAKE] that affected [WHO] for [DURATION]. Include: what happened, what it cost them, what I changed so it doesn't recur, and what I'm offering. No passive voice, no 'we regret any inconvenience'.
When To Use It: You actually broke something and need trust back
Expected Output: Apology email + a one-line internal note on the process fix

Prompt: Create an automated email for when [TRIGGER EVENT] happens in my business: welcome, delivery, review request, renewal reminder, payment failure. Give the copy and the timing.
When To Use It: You're doing by hand what should fire automatically
Expected Output: Email copy + trigger + send timing + one metric to watch

Prompt: Rewrite this so it reads warm and personal, not AI-written: vary sentence length, add one specific detail, remove every cliché, and let it sound slightly imperfect. Text: [PASTE EMAIL]
When To Use It: You can tell it's generated and so can they
Expected Output: Rewrite + the 3 clichés you'd delete from your own templates

Prompt: Write a newsletter intro for the [MONTH] edition covering [TOPICS]. Open with the single most interesting thing, not the summary. Under 100 words, then hand off to sections.
When To Use It: Monthly updates nobody reads
Expected Output: Intro + section-handoff lines

Prompt: Draft the email that says no to [REQUEST] without losing the relationship. State the decision, one honest reason, one alternative that helps them anyway.
When To Use It: The ask you keep sitting on because saying no is awkward
Expected Output: Decline email + a softer variant for a close relationship

Prompt: Write a re-engagement email for a mailing list that hasn't bought in [TIMEFRAME]. Segment it: those who opened recently, those who never opened, those who clicked but didn't buy.
When To Use It: A list going cold
Expected Output: 3 emails, one per segment, each with its own ask

Prompt: Turn a customer-support conversation into a public FAQ answer that pre-empts the same question 50 more times. Raw thread: [PASTE THREAD]
When To Use It: You're answering the same thing weekly
Expected Output: FAQ entry + the 3 places to publish it

Prompt: Write a reply to an unhappy customer who says [THEIR COMPLAINT]. Acknowledge the real feeling, own the specific part we got wrong, state exactly what happens next and when, and offer one reasonable make-good. No scripted empathy language.
When To Use It: The message that makes you pause before opening
Expected Output: Reply + a follow-up to send 3 days later

Prompt: Turn this complaint into a process fix: [COMPLAINT]. Identify the step that allowed it, the check that would have caught it, who owns that check, and what it costs to add.
When To Use It: You're getting the same complaint twice and that's a system bug
Expected Output: Root cause + control + owner + cost estimate

Prompt: Create a 5-answer refund policy for [BUSINESS TYPE] that is generous enough to be a selling point and specific enough to prevent abuse. Cover: time window, condition, who decides, how fast, and the escalating cases.
When To Use It: Your refund policy is either scaring buyers or costing you money
Expected Output: Policy text + the one-sentence version for the product page

Prompt: Write a response to a public negative review that is honest, non-defensive, and reads well to the hundred people who weren't there. Review: [PASTE REVIEW]
When To Use It: Any visible criticism on Google, Yelp, app stores, social
Expected Output: Public reply + private message to actually resolve it

Prompt: Build a customer onboarding path for [PRODUCT OR SERVICE] with 4 touchpoints in the first 14 days. Each must move them to a specific first-result milestone, not just notify them.
When To Use It: New customers go quiet in week one and churn in month two
Expected Output: Touchpoint table: day, channel, message goal, milestone reached

Prompt: Draft answers to the 10 questions [PRODUCT] customers ask before buying. Honest answers including the ones where the answer is 'no, not yet, here's the workaround'.
When To Use It: Every sales call reanswers the same list
Expected Output: FAQ with answers + the 2 questions you should answer proactively

Prompt: Write a check-in message for [CLIENT] at [MILESTONE] that surfaces problems before they become churn. Ask 4 questions, one about their internal politics, one about what we're failing at.
When To Use It: Between renewal conversations, when things seem fine
Expected Output: Message + the 4 questions + the red flags in their likely answers

Prompt: Create a tiered support response system for [BUSINESS TYPE]: what counts as urgent, response times by tier, what self-serves, and how to tell customers the difference without insulting them.
When To Use It: You're treating every message as priority one
Expected Output: Policy table + the customer-facing wording

Prompt: Rewrite these support macros so they sound like a competent person and not a template: keep each fix under 90 words, lead with the action the customer should take, and end with what happens next. Paste: [PASTE MACROS]
When To Use It: Your canned replies have drifted into robotic
Expected Output: Rewrites + the 3 phrases to retire permanently

Prompt: Prepare a response for a customer who says [THREAT]. Give me the de-escalation reply, the internal decision rule for when to concede, and the line I don't cross.
When To Use It: Confrontational moments where one bad reply goes public
Expected Output: Reply + decision rule + boundary wording

Prompt: Write a cancellation-flow set of messages for [SERVICE]: the confirm, the 'here's what you're losing', the data export offer, and the door-open note 60 days later. Respectful, no dark patterns.
When To Use It: People leaving and you want them back later
Expected Output: 4 messages with send timing

Prompt: Build a client intake questionnaire for [SERVICE] that catches scope problems before the work starts. 12 questions, ordered, with the reason each one exists and what a dangerous answer looks like.
When To Use It: Projects go wrong in week one because nobody asked
Expected Output: Questionnaire + red-flag answers

Prompt: Write plain-language documentation for [FEATURE OR PROCESS] aimed at someone who has used it once and forgot. Numbered steps, what each click does, what to do if it looks different.
When To Use It: You're training the same person twice
Expected Output: Doc + a troubleshooting table

Prompt: Draft a message to [CLIENT] explaining why a deadline moved. State the cause without blame-shifting, the new date, what you'll deliver by the old date anyway, and what you'd do in their position.
When To Use It: Delays you can't avoid and shouldn't sugarcoat
Expected Output: Email + an internal prevention note

Prompt: Create a feedback-collection loop for [BUSINESS TYPE]: 3 moments to ask, the one question at each, where the answers go, and how you close the loop so people keep answering.
When To Use It: You collect feedback nobody acts on and people stopped giving it
Expected Output: Loop design + question wording + the closing-the-loop message

Prompt: Write a one-page spec for [FEATURE] in [PRODUCT]: problem, who hits it, proposed behaviour, edge cases, what we're explicitly not building, and how we'll know it worked.
When To Use It: Before you let anyone write code or agree in a meeting
Expected Output: Spec + the 3 open questions to resolve first

Prompt: Prioritise this backlog with [METHOD] and show the scoring. Explain any item that ranked high on reach but low on effort-adjusted value. Backlog: [PASTE ITEMS]
When To Use It: Everything is urgent and you have limited capacity
Expected Output: Ranked table + scores + what you'd cut entirely

Prompt: Map the current process for [WORKFLOW] as steps, owners, handoffs, and waiting time. Then mark every step the customer would not pay for. Workflow: [DESCRIPTION]
When To Use It: You're slowing yourself down and can't see where
Expected Output: Process map + non-value-add list + the simplified version

Prompt: Write 5 user-interview question sets for [SEGMENT] that never mention my product and never lead the answer. Focus each set on one thing: their day, their workarounds, their spend, their failures, their vocabulary.
When To Use It: Before building anything, when you think you already know
Expected Output: 5 question sets + the follow-up prompt for a thin answer

Prompt: Turn these [N] pieces of user feedback into themes with counts, severity, and a recommendation per theme. Paste: [PASTE FEEDBACK]
When To Use It: You have 300 comments and no structure
Expected Output: Theme table + top 3 to act on + what to explicitly ignore

Prompt: Write acceptance criteria for [STORY OR TASK] in Given/When/Then form, including the failure paths and the two cases a tester will definitely miss.
When To Use It: Handing work over and getting the wrong thing back
Expected Output: Criteria + missing-test list

Prompt: Create a launch checklist for [RELEASE] covering: who to tell, what to update (docs, pricing page, macros), what to monitor in the first 48 hours, and the rollback trigger.
When To Use It: Every release, so nothing depends on your memory
Expected Output: Checklist with owners and timings

Prompt: Document this tool or subscription decision for [TOOL] for [USE CASE]: what it replaces, real cost including setup time, the risk of not having it, and a buy/don't-buy verdict with a date to review.
When To Use It: Your software stack has quietly become a monthly tax
Expected Output: One-page decision memo

Prompt: Design an automation for [REPEATABLE TASK] that I currently do by hand. Describe the trigger, the steps, what still needs a human, and what breaks when the automation fails silently.
When To Use It: You've done something manually more than 20 times
Expected Output: Automation design + failure handling + estimated hours saved per month

Prompt: Write a runbook for [INCIDENT TYPE]: detection, first 5 minutes, who to notify, decision points, recovery, and the post-incident questions. Assume the reader is awake at 3am and tired.
When To Use It: When something breaks and nobody remembers the procedure
Expected Output: Runbook + escalation contacts template

Prompt: Review my product page for [PRODUCT] against the 6 reasons people don't buy: unclear value, wrong audience, no proof, too much friction, hidden cost, no urgency. Paste: [PASTE PAGE]
When To Use It: Traffic without conversion
Expected Output: Audit with the single highest-leverage fix

Prompt: Create a weekly operating review template for [BUSINESS TYPE] that takes 20 minutes: 5 numbers, 1 blocked item, 1 decision, 1 customer insight, next week's single priority.
When To Use It: A rhythm so you stop firefighting
Expected Output: Template + what each number should trigger if it moves

Prompt: Write a data-collection plan for [DECISION]: what I currently know, what I'd need, the cheapest way to find out, and the threshold that would change my mind.
When To Use It: You're about to guess on something that's expensive to be wrong about
Expected Output: Plan + minimum viable evidence + decision threshold

Prompt: Document [PROCESS] so a new person can run it without asking me anything. Include the context they need, the steps, the judgement calls, and where it usually goes wrong.
When To Use It: Anything you're the only one who knows how to do
Expected Output: SOP written for a competent stranger

Prompt: Design a QA pass for [OFFER] before it goes live: the 15 things to check, in the order that catches the worst failures first.
When To Use It: Every launch, every page, every campaign
Expected Output: Checklist ordered by damage potential

Prompt: Build a pricing structure for [OFFER] with 3 tiers. Define who each tier is for, the honest difference in value, the anchor tier, and what to deliberately leave out of the cheapest one.
When To Use It: You're pricing on vibes and leaving money on the table
Expected Output: Tier table + reasoning + the sentence to explain pricing to a customer

Prompt: Analyse these numbers for [BUSINESS TYPE]: revenue [FIGURES], costs [COSTS], customers [COUNT]. Tell me my margin, contribution per customer, break-even, and the one line item that's disproportionate.
When To Use It: Monthly, before you make a spending decision
Expected Output: Metrics + the anomaly + what to investigate first

Prompt: Write the email that raises prices for [EXISTING CUSTOMERS]. Give the reason, the new price, the effective date, what stays the same, and one honest concession for early renewal.
When To Use It: The scariest email in a small business and the most profitable one
Expected Output: Email + objection replies for 'I'll leave' and 'this is too much'

Prompt: Calculate whether [SPEND DECISION] pays back. Show my assumptions, the break-even volume, and what has to be true for this to work. Numbers: [INPUTS]
When To Use It: Any spend you're defending to yourself
Expected Output: Payback model + assumptions list + the failure scenario

Prompt: Create a discount policy for [BUSINESS TYPE]: what justifies one, the maximum, who approves, what you never discount, and the alternative you offer instead of cutting price.
When To Use It: Discounts have become your default closing tool
Expected Output: Policy + 4 non-price concessions to offer instead

Prompt: Build a 13-week cash forecast structure for [BUSINESS] showing the rows I need, the assumptions to make explicit, and the warning threshold where I stop spending.
When To Use It: You don't know if you can afford the next quarter
Expected Output: Template columns + assumption list + trigger points

Prompt: Write a quote for [SCOPE OF WORK] at [PRICE] for [CLIENT]. Line items, what's included, what triggers a change-order charge, payment schedule, validity period, and the acceptance step.
When To Use It: Every job above a threshold price
Expected Output: Quote document + the change-order clause in plain English

Prompt: Compare [OPTION A] and [OPTION B] for [PURPOSE] across cost, time to value, lock-in, risk, and 3-year total. Then say which you'd pick and what would flip the decision.
When To Use It: Vendor choices, tools, build-vs-buy
Expected Output: Comparison table + recommendation + flip conditions

Prompt: Design a payment-terms structure for [BUSINESS TYPE] that protects my cash flow without pushing customers away: deposit, milestones, late handling, what to do about net-60 demands.
When To Use It: You're effectively financing your customers
Expected Output: Terms proposal + the negotiation script for pushback

Prompt: Turn my revenue into a unit-economics picture for [MODEL]: acquisition cost, first-purchase value, repeat rate, lifetime value, payback period. Use these inputs: [INPUTS]. Mark anything I'm guessing.
When To Use It: Before scaling spend, when growth feels fine but cash doesn't
Expected Output: Unit table + the weakest assumption + what to measure to confirm it

Prompt: Write a monthly financial review that a non-finance founder can run in 15 minutes for [BUSINESS TYPE]: the 6 numbers, what good looks like, and the question to ask when each one moves.
When To Use It: First of every month
Expected Output: Review template + thresholds + diagnostic questions

Prompt: Prepare for [COUNTERPARTY] over [SUBJECT]. My target, my floor, my walk-away, their likely ask, three trades I can make that cost me little, and the exact opening line.
When To Use It: Anything where the number is actually movable
Expected Output: Prep sheet + opening line + concession sequence

Prompt: Create an invoice and reminder sequence for [BUSINESS TYPE]: the invoice wording, day-7 nudge, day-14 firm notice, day-30 consequence, and how to keep the relationship.
When To Use It: Late payment is your biggest unmanaged risk
Expected Output: 5 templates with timing

Prompt: Identify the tax and record-keeping structure my [COUNTRY] business should have at [REVENUE] — entity type considerations, what to separate, what to track weekly, and what to ask an accountant. This is not tax advice, it's a question list.
When To Use It: Before revenue makes your setup wrong
Expected Output: Checklist + the 6 questions to bring to a professional

Prompt: Write a fundable one-page summary of [BUSINESS] for [BANK OR INVESTOR]: the model, the numbers that matter, the use of funds, and the risk you'd raise yourself.
When To Use It: You need outside money or a credit line
Expected Output: One-pager + the numbers to have ready

Prompt: Write a job post for [ROLE] that attracts the right person and filters the wrong one. Include the first 90 days, the actual problems, what success looks like in numbers, and the honest reasons it's hard.
When To Use It: Most job posts describe a wishlist, not a job
Expected Output: Post + 5 screening questions that reveal real capability

Prompt: Design a hiring test for [ROLE] that takes the candidate under 90 minutes, predicts real performance, and respects their time. Explain what each part measures.
When To Use It: You keep hiring on conversation and getting it wrong
Expected Output: Assessment design + what each part predicts + rubric

Prompt: Build an interview question set for [ROLE]: 4 for skill, 4 for judgement, 3 for motivation, 2 red-flag probes. Include the follow-up that gets past a rehearsed answer.
When To Use It: Structured interviews, so two candidates are comparable
Expected Output: Question set + what a strong and weak answer sounds like

Prompt: Write an onboarding plan for [NEW HIRE ROLE] covering week one, first month, first quarter. Each phase has the knowledge, the output, and the check-in. Name the two mistakes that lose people early.
When To Use It: Their first three weeks decide the next three years
Expected Output: Plan + the check-in conversation scripts

Prompt: Draft the difficult performance conversation with [TEAM MEMBER] about [ISSUE]. Facts not labels, the impact on others, the specific change required, the support offered, and the consequence with a date.
When To Use It: The conversation you keep postponing
Expected Output: Talking points + their likely responses + your replies

Prompt: Write a role brief for [ROLE] with: purpose, scope, decisions they own, decisions they escalate, who they work with, success metrics at 6 and 12 months.
When To Use It: Confusion about ownership costs more than bad hiring
Expected Output: One-page brief + the escalation list

Prompt: Create a compensation conversation script for [SITUATION] that is honest about constraints and specific about the path to more.
When To Use It: Money talks with people you want to keep
Expected Output: Script + the numbers to prepare + what not to promise

Prompt: Design a written weekly update format for a [TEAM SIZE]-person [TYPE] team: the 5 fields, what good looks like in each, and how to stop status meetings without losing visibility.
When To Use It: Meeties are your most expensive habit
Expected Output: Template + rules + the meeting to keep

Prompt: Write a firing or exit conversation plan for [REASON] that is legal-check safe, humane, clear, and protects the rest of the team's trust in you.
When To Use It: Nobody enjoys it and unprepared ones go badly
Expected Output: Plan + the exact words + what to tell the team afterwards

Prompt: Build a freelance contract brief for [PROJECT] with scope, deliverables, revision rounds, timeline, payment schedule, ownership of work, kill fee, and the out-of-scope list.
When To Use It: Scope creep starts in the first message, not the third
Expected Output: Brief + the clause that saves you most often

Prompt: Write the message to [CANDIDATE] declining them in a way that keeps them warm for [FUTURE ROLE] and doesn't embarrass either of us.
When To Use It: You'll want this person again
Expected Output: Decline message + a 6-month re-engagement note

Prompt: Create a team agreement for [TEAM] covering decision rights, response-time expectations, meeting norms, conflict handling, and how we say 'this isn't working'.
When To Use It: Culture problems are usually undefined-rule problems
Expected Output: Agreement + the facilitation questions to fill it in together

Prompt: Design a review-and-promotion framework for [TEAM TYPE] with levels defined by impact and judgement rather than tenure, and evidence each person should be collecting.
When To Use It: Your best people can't see a path and start looking
Expected Output: Framework + evidence list + the review conversation template

Prompt: Write a recruiting outreach message to [PASSIVE CANDIDATE PROFILE] that doesn't read like a recruiter blast. Reference something specific, name the actual problem they'd work on, be honest about why the role exists, ask one question.
When To Use It: Good people who aren't looking
Expected Output: Message + subject + follow-up for silence

Prompt: Build a documentation habit for a [TEAM SIZE]-person team: which 5 docs matter, who updates them, when the review happens, and how to make writing one cheaper than skipping it.
When To Use It: Every hire reinvents what's in someone's head
Expected Output: Doc list + ownership + cadence + the incentive that makes it stick

Prompt: Research [MARKET OR SEGMENT] for [PURPOSE]. Give me: who the buyers are, what they currently use, what they complain about, typical price points, the 3 gaps, and what evidence I should verify myself before acting.
When To Use It: Before entering a market or launching to a segment
Expected Output: Brief + gaps + a verification checklist (mark every unverified claim)

Prompt: Analyse [COMPETITOR] for [MY OFFER]: their positioning, apparent pricing, who they clearly win with, where they're weak, and the three most credible ways I differentiate without attacking them.
When To Use It: You're copying their page instead of answering them
Expected Output: Competitive breakdown + positioning options + what to avoid claiming

Prompt: Run a [FRAMEWORK] analysis of [BUSINESS TYPE] in [MARKET], then ignore the obvious cells and tell me the two items that actually change a decision and why.
When To Use It: Annual planning, big pivots, new markets
Expected Output: Analysis + the decision-relevant subset + what it implies for the next quarter

Prompt: Stress-test this plan: [PLAN]. Give me the assumptions it depends on, the three most likely ways it fails, the earliest warning signal for each, and the cheapest test to run before committing.
When To Use It: Before you spend real money on a strategy
Expected Output: Assumption list + failure modes + early signals + tests

Prompt: Build a decision matrix for [CHOICE] with the criteria that actually matter for [CONTEXT], their weights and my reasoning, scored options, and a sensitivity note on which criterion flips the answer.
When To Use It: Any two-option decision you've made twice already
Expected Output: Matrix + weights rationale + flip condition

Prompt: Summarise the state of [TOPIC] for a [ROLE] who needs to make a decision this week, not become an expert. Separate established facts, active debate, and open unknowns. Name what's most likely to change in 12 months.
When To Use It: New domain, fast, without pretending to know it
Expected Output: Brief with fact/debate/unknown split + decision implications + the citation list to verify

Prompt: Design a 2-week validation experiment for this hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS]. Define the minimum audience, the single metric, the pass threshold, the kill threshold, and the total cost ceiling.
When To Use It: You're about to build something nobody confirmed they want
Expected Output: Experiment spec + interpretation guide + what to build if it passes

Prompt: Map my customer segments for [BUSINESS] from these inputs: [DATA]. Group by job-to-be-done, size each, note who's most profitable versus who's easiest to reach, and name which two to focus on and what to stop doing for the rest.
When To Use It: You're marketing to everyone and resonating with nobody
Expected Output: Segment table + focus recommendation + explicit non-target list

Prompt: Write a strategy memo for [DECISION] using situation, implication, options, recommendation, risks, and what we'd need to see to reverse it. One page, decision-maker voice. Inputs: [INPUTS]
When To Use It: Anything that needs a written position, not a meeting
Expected Output: Memo + the reversal triggers

Prompt: Identify the 5 highest-leverage constraints in [BUSINESS] right now given these numbers: [FIGURES]. For each: how I know it's the constraint, what removing it releases, and the cost of trying.
When To Use It: Growth stalls and everyone blames marketing
Expected Output: Ranked constraints + test for each + what not to do

Prompt: Research the [REGULATORY OR COMPLIANCE] requirements for [ACTIVITY] in [COUNTRY]. What applies to a business of [SIZE], what's commonly missed, the penalties, and the questions for a professional.
Variables to Fill: ACTIVITY, COUNTRY, REGULATORY OR COMPLIANCE, SIZE
When To Use It: Anything involving data, money, health, food, or cross-border selling
Expected Output: Requirements summary + gaps + professional question list (not legal advice)

Prompt: Do a post-mortem on [COMPLETED PROJECT OR PERIOD]. Separate outcome from process, quantify what actually moved, what was luck, what I'd repeat, and the one habit to retire.
When To Use It: After every launch and every quarter
Expected Output: Post-mortem + repeat/stop list + the number to track next time

Prompt: Build a 12-month plan for [GOAL] backwards from the deadline: the 4 quarterly milestones, the monthly evidence each produces, the dependency chain, and the two things I must say no to.
When To Use It: Planning season, or when you're busy without progressing
Expected Output: Milestone map + dependencies + the explicit no-list

Prompt: Compare [CHANNEL A] and [CHANNEL B] for [OFFER] given my constraints: [TIME], [BUDGET], [SKILLS]. Expected cost per customer, time to first signal, and what must be true for each to work.
Variables to Fill: BUDGET, CHANNEL A, CHANNEL B, OFFER, SKILLS, TIME
When To Use It: You can only run one marketing channel properly right now
Expected Output: Comparison + recommendation + the review date and kill criteria

Prompt: Write a weekly competitive and market digest for [INDUSTRY] that takes me 10 minutes: the 5 things to track, where to look, what signals a threat, and what's noise I should ignore.
When To Use It: Stay informed without doomscrolling
Expected Output: Digest template + sources + threat signals vs noise
